chunk.section: Statement of Work No. 1 - Data Migration
chunk.text:
This Statement of Work ("SOW") is issued under the Master Services Agreement dated January 15, 2024 between Acme Corporation ("Provider") and Northwind Logistics Inc. ("Customer"). It describes the migration of Customer's shipment-tracking data from its legacy on-premises system to Enterprise Cloud.

1. Scope

Provider will extract, transform and load approximately 40 million shipment records and 1.2 terabytes of attached documents from Customer's legacy Oracle database into Enterprise Cloud, and will validate record counts and checksums after each load.

2. Out of Scope

Migration of archived records older than seven (7) years, changes to Customer's internal reporting tools, and end-user training are not included in this SOW.

3. Timeline

The project runs for twelve (12) weeks starting March 3, 2025. The cutover to production is planned for the weekend of May 24, 2025.

4. Fees and Milestones

The fixed fee for this SOW is US$85,000, invoiced on completion of three milestones:

Milestone 1, approved migration plan: 30% of the fee.

Milestone 2, successful test migration in the staging environment: 40% of the fee.

Milestone 3, production cutover accepted by Customer: 30% of the fee.

Travel expenses are billed separately at cost and may not exceed US$6,000 without Customer's written approval.

5. Acceptance

Customer has ten (10) business days after each milestone delivery to accept it or to describe in writing how it does not meet this SOW. A milestone not rejected within that period is deemed accepted.

6. Change Requests

Any change to scope, timeline or fees requires a written change request signed by both parties. Provider will estimate the impact of a requested change within five (5) business days.

7. Project Contacts

Provider's project manager is Lena Park. Customer's project sponsor is Tom Becker, Chief Operating Officer.

This handbook summarizes the principal policies for employees of Acme Corporation. It is an internal document and does not form part of any customer agreement.

## Paid Time Off
Employees are entitled to twenty-five (25) days of paid time off per calendar year, accruing monthly. Up to five (5) unused days may be carried over into the following year.

## Working Model
Acme operates a hybrid working model. Employees must work from the office a minimum of two (2) days per week, with core collaboration hours between 10:00 and 16:00 local time.

## Probation
New employees serve a probationary period of three (3) months, during which either party may end the employment with one (1) week's notice.

2. Sick Leave

Employees receive ten (10) days of paid sick leave per calendar year. Sick leave does not carry over to the following year. A medical certificate is required for an absence of more than three (3) consecutive working days.

3. Bereavement Leave

Employees receive up to five (5) days of paid bereavement leave on the death of an immediate family member, and up to two (2) days for an extended family member.

4. Jury Duty

Employees called for jury duty receive full pay for up to ten (10) working days per year.

5. Sabbatical

After five (5) years of continuous employment, employees may take a paid sabbatical of four (4) weeks. A sabbatical must be requested at least three (3) months in advance and approved by the employee's manager.

6. Unpaid Leave

Unpaid leave of up to three (3) months may be granted at the company's discretion. Health insurance continues during approved unpaid leave.

Employees book economy class for flights scheduled at six (6) hours or less. Business class is allowed for flights scheduled at more than six (6) hours, with the approval of a Vice President. Tickets should be booked at least fourteen (14) days before departure when possible.

chunk.section: 2. Passwords and Authentication
chunk.text:
Passwords must be at least fourteen (14) characters long. Multi-factor authentication is required for every company system that supports it, including email, source control and the VPN. Passwords are not rotated on a schedule; they must be changed immediately when a compromise is suspected.

3. Devices

Company laptops must use full-disk encryption, automatic screen lock after five (5) minutes of inactivity and the managed endpoint protection agent. Lost or stolen devices must be reported to the IT service desk within four (4) hours.

4. Access Control

Access is granted on a least-privilege basis and reviewed every quarter by the system owner. Access for departing employees is revoked on their last working day.

5. Incident Reporting

Employees must report any suspected security incident to security@acme.example within one (1) hour of noticing it. The security team classifies incidents by severity and leads the response.

6. Training

All employees complete security awareness training when they join and every year after that. Employees who fail a simulated phishing test complete a short refresher course within fourteen (14) days.

7. Vendors

A vendor that will process Confidential or Restricted data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. The review is repeated every two (2) years.

8. Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy require written approval from the Chief Information Security Officer and expire after twelve (12) months.

Employees who travel more than four (4) times per year are issued a corporate card. Personal expenses must never be charged to it.

## 3. Data Location and International Transfers
Personal data is stored in data centers located in Frankfurt, Germany (European Union) and in Virginia, United States. Transfers of personal data from the EU to the US are carried out under the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses.

## 4. Security Measures
Provider encrypts personal data at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher. Access to production data is restricted to authorized personnel on a least-privilege basis.

## 5. Breach Notification
Provider will notify the Controller of any confirmed personal-data breach within seventy-two (72) hours of discovery, and will cooperate with the Controller's investigation and remediation.

## 6. Data Subject Requests
Provider will assist the Controller in responding to data-subject requests (access, rectification, erasure) and will forward any such request it receives directly to the Controller within five (5) business days.

## 7. Retention and Deletion
Upon termination of the Agreement, Provider will delete all personal data processed on the Controller's behalf within ninety (90) days, unless retention is required by applicable law.

The Controller may audit Provider's compliance with this DPA once per calendar year, on at least thirty (30) days' written notice.

Purchases above US$50,000 require at least three (3) written quotes, unless the supplier is the only one able to provide the goods or services. A sole-source justification must then be attached to the purchase order.

## 3. Vendor Onboarding

New suppliers are onboarded by the Procurement team. A supplier that will access company or customer data must also pass the security review described in the Information Security Policy before the contract is signed.

## 4. Payment Terms

Acme's standard payment term for suppliers is forty-five (45) days from the invoice date. Shorter terms require approval from the Finance business partner.

Splitting a purchase into smaller orders to avoid an approval threshold is prohibited.

This Statement of Work ("SOW") is issued under the Master Services Agreement dated January 15, 2024 between Acme Corporation ("Provider") and Northwind Logistics Inc. ("Customer"). Provider will extract, transform and load approximately 40 million shipment records and 1.2 terabytes of attached documents from Customer's legacy Oracle database into Enterprise Cloud, and will validate record counts and checksums after each load.

Milestone 1, approved migration plan: 30% of the fee.

Milestone 3, production cutover accepted by Customer: 30% of the fee.

Travel expenses are billed separately at cost and may not exceed US$6,000 without Customer's written approval.

5. Acceptance

Customer has ten (10) business days after each milestone delivery to accept it or to describe in writing how it does not meet this SOW. A milestone not rejected within that period is deemed accepted.

6. Change Requests

Any change to scope, timeline or fees requires a written change request signed by both parties. Provider will estimate the impact of a requested change within five (5) business days.

7. Project Contacts

Provider's project manager is Lena Park. Customer's project sponsor is Tom Becker, Chief Operating Officer.

chunk.section: Statement of Work No. 1 - Data Migration
chunk.text:
This Statement of Work ("SOW") is issued under the Master Services Agreement dated January 15, 2024 between Acme Corporation ("Provider") and Northwind Logistics Inc. ("Customer"). It describes the migration of Customer's shipment-tracking data from its legacy on-premises system to Enterprise Cloud.

1. Scope

Provider will extract, transform and load approximately 40 million shipment records and 1.2 terabytes of attached documents from Customer's legacy Oracle database into Enterprise Cloud, and will validate record counts and checksums after each load.

2. Out of Scope

Migration of archived records older than seven (7) years, changes to Customer's internal reporting tools, and end-user training are not included in this SOW.

3. Timeline

The project runs for twelve (12) weeks starting March 3, 2025. The cutover to production is planned for the weekend of May 24, 2025.

4. Fees and Milestones

The fixed fee for this SOW is US$85,000, invoiced on completion of three milestones:

Milestone 1, approved migration plan: 30% of the fee.

Milestone 2, successful test migration in the staging environment: 40% of the fee.

Milestone 3, production cutover accepted by Customer: 30% of the fee.

Travel expenses are billed separately at cost and may not exceed US$6,000 without Customer's written approval.

5. Acceptance

Customer has ten (10) business days after each milestone delivery to accept it or to describe in writing how it does not meet this SOW. A milestone not rejected within that period is deemed accepted.

6. Change Requests

Any change to scope, timeline or fees requires a written change request signed by both parties. Provider will estimate the impact of a requested change within five (5) business days.

7. Project Contacts

Provider's project manager is Lena Park. Customer's project sponsor is Tom Becker, Chief Operating Officer.

A vendor that will process Confidential or Restricted data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. The review is repeated every two (2) years.

Exceptions to this policy require written approval from the Chief Information Security Officer and expire after twelve (12) months.

# Service Level Agreement

This Service Level Agreement ("SLA") applies to the services provided by Acme Corporation under the Master Services Agreement.

## 1. Uptime Commitment
Provider commits to a monthly uptime of 99.9% for the production service. Uptime is measured per calendar month and excludes scheduled maintenance windows.

chunk.section: 2. Passwords and Authentication
chunk.text:
Passwords must be at least fourteen (14) characters long. Multi-factor authentication is required for every company system that supports it, including email, source control and the VPN. Passwords are not rotated on a schedule; they must be changed immediately when a compromise is suspected.

3. Devices

Company laptops must use full-disk encryption, automatic screen lock after five (5) minutes of inactivity and the managed endpoint protection agent. Lost or stolen devices must be reported to the IT service desk within four (4) hours.

4. Access Control

Access is granted on a least-privilege basis and reviewed every quarter by the system owner. Access for departing employees is revoked on their last working day.

5. Incident Reporting

Employees must report any suspected security incident to security@acme.example within one (1) hour of noticing it. The security team classifies incidents by severity and leads the response.

6. Training

All employees complete security awareness training when they join and every year after that. Employees who fail a simulated phishing test complete a short refresher course within fourteen (14) days.

7. Vendors

A vendor that will process Confidential or Restricted data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. The review is repeated every two (2) years.

8. Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy require written approval from the Chief Information Security Officer and expire after twelve (12) months.

Employees are entitled to twenty-five (25) days of paid time off per calendar year, accruing monthly. Up to five (5) unused days may be carried over into the following year.

Acme operates a hybrid working model. Employees must work from the office a minimum of two (2) days per week, with core collaboration hours between 10:00 and 16:00 local time.

New employees serve a probationary period of three (3) months, during which either party may end the employment with one (1) week's notice.

After probation, employees are asked to give at least one (1) month's written notice of resignation.

## Business Expenses
Pre-approved business expenses are reimbursed within thirty (30) days of a complete expense claim.

chunk.text:
This Statement of Work ("SOW") is issued under the Master Services Agreement dated January 15, 2024 between Acme Corporation ("Provider") and Northwind Logistics Inc. ("Customer"). It describes the migration of Customer's shipment-tracking data from its legacy on-premises system to Enterprise Cloud.

1. Scope

Provider will extract, transform and load approximately 40 million shipment records and 1.2 terabytes of attached documents from Customer's legacy Oracle database into Enterprise Cloud, and will validate record counts and checksums after each load.

2. Out of Scope

Migration of archived records older than seven (7) years, changes to Customer's internal reporting tools, and end-user training are not included in this SOW.

3. Timeline

The project runs for twelve (12) weeks starting March 3, 2025. The cutover to production is planned for the weekend of May 24, 2025.

The fixed fee for this SOW is US$85,000, invoiced on completion of three milestones:

Milestone 1, approved migration plan: 30% of the fee.

Milestone 2, successful test migration in the staging environment: 40% of the fee.

Milestone 3, production cutover accepted by Customer: 30% of the fee.

Travel expenses are billed separately at cost and may not exceed US$6,000 without Customer's written approval.

5. Acceptance

Customer has ten (10) business days after each milestone delivery to accept it or to describe in writing how it does not meet this SOW. A milestone not rejected within that period is deemed accepted.

6. Change Requests

Any change to scope, timeline or fees requires a written change request signed by both parties. Provider will estimate the impact of a requested change within five (5) business days.

7. Project Contacts

Provider's project manager is Lena Park. Customer's project sponsor is Tom Becker, Chief Operating Officer.

Upon termination of the Agreement, Provider will delete all personal data processed on the Controller's behalf within ninety (90) days, unless retention is required by applicable law.

The Controller may audit Provider's compliance with this DPA once per calendar year, on at least thirty (30) days' written notice.

## 1. Approval Thresholds

Every purchase requires a purchase order approved according to its total contract value:

- below US$10,000: the requester's manager;
- from US$10,000 to US$100,000: a Director and the Finance business partner;
- above US$100,000 and up to US$500,000: the Chief Financial Officer;
- above US$500,000: the Chief Executive Officer, after review by the Chief Financial Officer.

## 2. Competitive Quotes

Purchases above US$50,000 require at least three (3) written quotes, unless the supplier is the only one able to provide the goods or services. A sole-source justification must then be attached to the purchase order.

## 3. Vendor Onboarding

New suppliers are onboarded by the Procurement team. A supplier that will access company or customer data must also pass the security review described in the Information Security Policy before the contract is signed.

Acme's standard payment term for suppliers is forty-five (45) days from the invoice date. Shorter terms require approval from the Finance business partner.

Splitting a purchase into smaller orders to avoid an approval threshold is prohibited.

This Statement of Work ("SOW") is issued under the Master Services Agreement dated January 15, 2024 between Acme Corporation ("Provider") and Northwind Logistics Inc. ("Customer"). It describes the migration of Customer's shipment-tracking data from its legacy on-premises system to Enterprise Cloud.

1. Scope

Provider will extract, transform and load approximately 40 million shipment records and 1.2 terabytes of attached documents from Customer's legacy Oracle database into Enterprise Cloud, and will validate record counts and checksums after each load.

2. Out of Scope

Migration of archived records older than seven (7) years, changes to Customer's internal reporting tools, and end-user training are not included in this SOW.

3. Timeline

The project runs for twelve (12) weeks starting March 3, 2025. The cutover to production is planned for the weekend of May 24, 2025.

4. Fees and Milestones

The fixed fee for this SOW is US$85,000, invoiced on completion of three milestones:

Milestone 1, approved migration plan: 30% of the fee.

Milestone 2, successful test migration in the staging environment: 40% of the fee.

Milestone 3, production cutover accepted by Customer: 30% of the fee.

Travel expenses are billed separately at cost and may not exceed US$6,000 without Customer's written approval.

5. Acceptance

Customer has ten (10) business days after each milestone delivery to accept it or to describe in writing how it does not meet this SOW. A milestone not rejected within that period is deemed accepted.

6. Change Requests

Any change to scope, timeline or fees requires a written change request signed by both parties. Provider will estimate the impact of a requested change within five (5) business days.

7. Project Contacts

Provider's project manager is Lena Park. Customer's project sponsor is Tom Becker, Chief Operating Officer.

## 2. Conflicts of Interest

Employees must disclose to Compliance any financial interest in a supplier, customer or competitor, and any outside employment, before it begins. Employees may not take part in a decision that involves a company in which they or a family member hold an interest.

Employees who hold material non-public information about Acme or another company may not trade in that company's securities, or advise others to do so.

chunk.section: 2. Passwords and Authentication
chunk.text:
Passwords must be at least fourteen (14) characters long. Multi-factor authentication is required for every company system that supports it, including email, source control and the VPN. Passwords are not rotated on a schedule; they must be changed immediately when a compromise is suspected.

3. Devices

Company laptops must use full-disk encryption, automatic screen lock after five (5) minutes of inactivity and the managed endpoint protection agent. Lost or stolen devices must be reported to the IT service desk within four (4) hours.

4. Access Control

Access is granted on a least-privilege basis and reviewed every quarter by the system owner. Access for departing employees is revoked on their last working day.

5. Incident Reporting

Employees must report any suspected security incident to security@acme.example within one (1) hour of noticing it. The security team classifies incidents by severity and leads the response.

6. Training

All employees complete security awareness training when they join and every year after that. Employees who fail a simulated phishing test complete a short refresher course within fourteen (14) days.

7. Vendors

A vendor that will process Confidential or Restricted data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. The review is repeated every two (2) years.

8. Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy require written approval from the Chief Information Security Officer and expire after twelve (12) months.

New suppliers are onboarded by the Procurement team. A supplier that will access company or customer data must also pass the security review described in the Information Security Policy before the contract is signed.

Acme's standard payment term for suppliers is forty-five (45) days from the invoice date. Shorter terms require approval from the Finance business partner.

Splitting a purchase into smaller orders to avoid an approval threshold is prohibited.

This Statement of Work ("SOW") is issued under the Master Services Agreement dated January 15, 2024 between Acme Corporation ("Provider") and Northwind Logistics Inc. ("Customer"). It describes the migration of Customer's shipment-tracking data from its legacy on-premises system to Enterprise Cloud.

1. Scope

Provider will extract, transform and load approximately 40 million shipment records and 1.2 terabytes of attached documents from Customer's legacy Oracle database into Enterprise Cloud, and will validate record counts and checksums after each load.

2. Out of Scope

Migration of archived records older than seven (7) years, changes to Customer's internal reporting tools, and end-user training are not included in this SOW.

3. Timeline

The project runs for twelve (12) weeks starting March 3, 2025. The cutover to production is planned for the weekend of May 24, 2025.

4. Fees and Milestones

The fixed fee for this SOW is US$85,000, invoiced on completion of three milestones:

Milestone 1, approved migration plan: 30% of the fee.

Milestone 2, successful test migration in the staging environment: 40% of the fee.

Milestone 3, production cutover accepted by Customer: 30% of the fee.

Travel expenses are billed separately at cost and may not exceed US$6,000 without Customer's written approval.

5. Acceptance

Customer has ten (10) business days after each milestone delivery to accept it or to describe in writing how it does not meet this SOW. A milestone not rejected within that period is deemed accepted.

6. Change Requests

Any change to scope, timeline or fees requires a written change request signed by both parties. Provider will estimate the impact of a requested change within five (5) business days.

7. Project Contacts

Provider's project manager is Lena Park. Customer's project sponsor is Tom Becker, Chief Operating Officer.
